title: Gate command and gates.json: the transition from the document's state, the checks per gate, the findings format, evidence reproduction (P10)
description: Why: bead-loop runs one gate command in the worktree after the worker commits, with no bead id; the command must find what changed and know which gate applies (delivery-pipeline.md §5.4, §5.6). node pipeline/gate.mjs: diff against the base branch (BASE env or upstream/main), collect changed *.deck.json (workbench target) or changed contents.lr pages and the documents that generated them (lektor target, documents read from $WORKBENCH), read each document's state, run the gate for the implied transition from pipeline/gates.json ({gate: {blocking: [ids], advisory: [ids]}}), print one finding per line as 'CHECK CODE <prop> slide N: message → fix', exit 1 on any blocking finding. P10: recompute every evidence entry's report_sha and fail on mismatch. Findings text is snapshot-tested so a wording change is a deliberate commit. Portable: node and npm only, no flox dependence; geomlib internals via a checkout of brownnrl/euclid at pipeline/pins.json when a check needs them.
acceptance_criteria: in a worktree with one changed drafted document, node pipeline/gate.mjs runs exactly G1's checks and exits 0 on the Book IV IV.1 document; a seeded fault gives exit 1 with one line naming the slide; an evidence entry with a wrong sha fails P10; pipeline/test/gate.test.mjs passes.

title: XI.11 rotation: file the issue, fix rigid rotation about the pivot, add a rigid-motion invariants harness over the XI–XIII fixtures
description: Why: Nelson described it on euclid#155 (points slide along a rotated plane; F/G/H betweenness flips) and every 3D deck inherits it (delivery-pipeline.md §6.1, PLAN.md P1). Reproduce first on content/elements/books/bookXI/propositions/propXI11 (pivot F,xyplane) headlessly: build the slate from the param strings, call rotateCoordinates for a small drag, and measure the invariants. The harness is the deliverable that outlives the fix: tests/RigidMotionTest.ts loads every view/euclid-html/bookxi*, bookxii*, bookxiii* fixture with a plane pivot, applies k rotations, and asserts pairwise point distances, foot-on-plane and slider-on-sphere incidences, and the sign of every ordered triple's betweenness are preserved to 1e-6. Then the fix in Slate.rotateCoordinates / the preexists skip (src/Slate.ts:1158-1196, 840-842) — one thing per PR: issue with the reproduction first, harness PR second (it will be red), fix PR third. Files (euclid worktree): tests/RigidMotionTest.ts, src/Slate.ts, doc/architecture.md drag-pipeline section if the semantics change.
acceptance_criteria: issue opened on brownnrl/euclid with the headless reproduction pasted; the harness fails on upstream main at the XI.11 fixture and passes with the fix; npm run test:unit and test:snapshot green; the snapshot goldens for 2D fixtures are bit-for-bit unchanged.

title: narrative-diff: prove the prose outside <figure> is unchanged modulo {NAME} tokens
description: Why: 'the narrative never changes' is the one rule that must not be broken and today it is enforced by reading (delivery-pipeline.md §4). Given a contents.lr before and after a deck edit: strip every block, replace {NAME}, {DISPLAY|NAME}, {NAME:canvas_N} tokens with their display text (lektor-eucrefs ELEM_REF_RE grammar, docs/research/lektor-content-pipeline.md §3), leave [!just …] directives in place, normalise whitespace, and require equality. Report the first differing line with context. Also usable as an upstream-facing check: run it over any lektor PR diff. Files: pipeline/narrative-diff.mjs, pipeline/test/narrative-diff.test.mjs, package.json script check:narrative.
acceptance_criteria: node --test passes with cases for: tokenizing existing letters (pass), adding a word (fail), removing a word (fail), a moved figure (pass), a changed [!just] (fail); running it over lektor PR #35's diff (git show on the sibling checkout) reports what it finds and the finding is either zero or explained in the close note.

title: Planning-table renderer and conversion of the sixteen Book IV tables into deck documents
description: Why: after this, the markdown table is output and the document is source (delivery-pipeline.md §3.2). Renderer: deck document → the seven-column table in lektor/doc/process.md format, with Shown/hidden written as deltas (+X, −X, (inherit)) computed from absolute visible arrays, Justs as 'claim — ref' pairs, animations in string form, and the header block (canvas, existing elements, deferDraggables, figure additions) as works/euclid-elements/book-iv/README.md already writes it. Conversion: works/euclid-elements/book-iv/propIV1.md … propIV16.md → works/euclid-elements/decks/bookIV/propIV*.deck.json, state=drafted; the open questions in book-iv/README.md move to a review.questions field. Then regenerate the markdown from the documents and diff against the hand-written tables; differences are either renderer bugs or table typos, each fixed at its source. Files: pipeline/render-table.mjs, works/euclid-elements/decks/bookIV/*.deck.json, works/euclid-elements/book-iv/*.md (regenerated), book-iv/README.md (one line: generated, do not edit).
acceptance_criteria: for every propIV*.deck.json, node pipeline/render-table.mjs produces the committed propIV*.md byte-for-byte; node pipeline/check-plan.mjs passes on all sixteen or every finding is listed in the bead's close note as a table fix sent for review.

title: Deck document v0: JSON Schema plus plan checks (names, captions, refs, animation names)
description: Why: the deck exists only as executed JS and its plan only as a markdown table (delivery-pipeline.md §2.1). Define schema deck/0 exactly over what ISlide reads (text, visible, highlighted, transition, justifications — euclid src/index.ts:222-228) plus figure_additions, aliases, deferDraggables, not_yet_implemented, state, review. Plan checks, each a function with its own test: (a) every name in visible/highlighted/elem and every {NAME} caption token resolves in figure ∪ figure_additions, aliases followed one hop like slideshow.ts canonicaliseSlideNames; (b) every caption is an in-order word run of one narrative sentence — port the in_order_fraction logic from lektor/scripts/check-captions.py, threshold 0.92, report the sentence matched; (c) every justification ref resolves with the lektor-eucrefs resolver rules (@I.5, I.Def.10, I.Post.3, C.N.1, X.Def.II.3, I.15.Cor); (d) every animation name is one of the 14 registered string names (docs/research/geomlib-internals.md §1.1) and its element type matches; (e) not_yet_implemented is empty or each entry names a brownnrl/euclid issue. Figure input: a figure.json extracted from contents.lr param strings (name;type;ctor;args). Files: pipeline/schema/deck-0.json, pipeline/check-plan.mjs, pipeline/extract-figure.mjs, pipeline/test/*.test.mjs, package.json scripts check:plan.
acceptance_criteria: node --test pipeline/test passes; node pipeline/check-plan.mjs works/euclid-elements/decks/bookIV/propIV1.deck.json prints zero findings on a correct document and one finding per seeded fault when a name, caption word, ref, or animation is changed.
notes: Revised 2026-09-21: the document also carries slides[].sentence (index into narrative.json), evidence[] ({id, verdict, inputs{document_sha,page_sha,geomlib_commit,flox_lock_sha}, report_sha}) and known_failures[] ({check, code, location, issue, expires}); plan checks are P1–P9 as catalogued in delivery-pipeline.md §5.3, each with seeded-fault fixtures (X2).

title: Delivery pipeline framework: deck document lifecycle, plan/render checks, generator, corpus visual run (docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §3–5)
description: Why: 403 decks remain and every stage of Nelson's process exists once, by hand (docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §1–2). This epic builds the pipeline that moves a proposition drafted → planned → approved → implemented → verified → delivered with a machine check at each stage, so throughput is bounded by his review only. Code lives in this repo under pipeline/ and runs geomlib from the euclid source checkout (the bundle exports neither Slate nor computeSlideState). Children are the stages; order: document + plan checks + table renderer first (Book IV conversion), then narrative-diff, generator, headless renderer, corpus run, bead generator, lektor CI PR.
acceptance_criteria: Book IV (16 props) goes through every child stage end to end: deck documents in works/euclid-elements/decks/bookIV/, generated tables identical in content to the reviewed ones, generated contents.lr edits pass check-decks.js and narrative-diff, a contact sheet per deck exists, and a PR body is produced for brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor.

title: 3D capabilities for Books XI–XIII: rigid rotation fix and invariants harness, solid-geometry animations, depth cues, per-slide view (docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §6)
description: Why: 75 propositions, 90 canvases, 54 using 3D-only constructions; the library has a 3D model but orthographic implicit projection, model-rotation via pivot with the XI.11 bug (euclid#155 comment), no depth handling, and zero 3D animations (14 registered, all 2D). Each tier is a design issue on brownnrl/euclid before code, per Nelson's rule. Tiers 0–2 run in parallel with Books III–X decks because XI–XIII are last in his backlog (lektor#29–31).
acceptance_criteria: Tier 0 merged upstream (XI.11 fix + invariants harness in euclid tests); design issues opened and answered for Tiers 1 and 2; a Book XI planning table can be written with an empty 'Not yet implemented' column.

title: .agents/skills: euclid-fidelity and euclid-verify — Nelson's rules and how to prove a change, in the form the bead-loop worker reads
description: Two skills under .agents/skills/ of this repo, each a SKILL.md with the frontmatter opencode needs (name, description; see ~/src/bead-loop/test/lint-skills.sh for the exact check), written for a model working a worktree of ~/src/euclid or ~/src/euclids-elements-lektor with these linked in (bead-loop bl-3x2 links them; until then the workflow skill's 'repo's own skills' sentence finds them only when the worker is told the path). euclid-fidelity: the original narrative never changes; a gray area gets a footnote, never an edit; Green Lion Press Heath is the reference; only slideshow captions are ours to write, and those are Joyce's sentence tokenized; one thing per PR; a design issue before code on anything larger than a bug; no rewrites proposed; the repo's AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md win on code style; Co-Authored-By trailers are fine (Nelson uses them). euclid-verify: for ~/src/euclid — npm ci, then npm test, with the LD_LIBRARY_PATH and NODE_OPTIONS quirk from PLAN.md and where it stops being needed; for the lektor repo — node check-decks.js and what it assumes about sibling checkouts; what a passing run prints; what to do when a test needs a browser. Keep each under 60 lines; the worker reads them every round. Files: .agents/skills/euclid-fidelity/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/euclid-verify/SKILL.md, CONTEXT.md (one line each under the vocabulary, if it lists skills).
acceptance_criteria: bash ~/src/bead-loop/test/lint-skills.sh run against this repo's .agents/skills (or its check reproduced: name and description present, name matches the directory) passes for both; every rule in euclid-fidelity traces to Nelson's #155 comment or PLAN.md; the commands in euclid-verify run green in a fresh worktree of ~/src/euclid on this box, as shown by pasting the last five lines of output into the bead's close note.

title: .bead-loop.toml: targets euclid and lektor — worktrees off upstream, PRs on brownnrl's repos via our forks, external merge, ask before opening
description: Blocked on bead-loop's targets epic (bl-wbo in ~/src/bead-loop; design in bead-loop docs/design-targets.md) — this bead is the config that epic exists for. Write .bead-loop.toml at the root of this repo: label = 'delegate:local', target_label = 'work' (the pw beads already carry work:euclid / work:lektor). [targets.euclid]: path = '~/src/euclid', base = 'main', base_remote = 'upstream', push_remote = 'origin' (imkarrer/euclid), pr_repo = 'brownnrl/euclid', merge = 'external', open_pr = 'ask', pr_style = 'plain', max_inflight = 1, setup and gate that pass in a fresh git worktree of ~/src/euclid (npm ci with the LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<util-linux.lib>/lib and NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-strip-types quirk from PLAN.md, or flox activate -d ~/src/euclid -- ... once that env exists; the worktree has no node_modules and no .flox). [targets.lektor]: fork brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor first (gh repo fork --remote in ~/src/euclids-elements-lektor renames brownnrl's remote to upstream and adds origin = imkarrer's fork), then path = '~/src/euclids-elements-lektor', pr_repo = 'brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor', same merge/open_pr/pr_style/max_inflight, gate = node check-decks.js (the scripts assume ../euclid and ../euclids-elements.org as siblings — a worktree under ~/.local/state/bead-loop/preservation-workbench/wt/ID breaks that; setup must symlink or the gate must cd; say which in the file). Add ~/src/preservation-workbench to repos in ~/.config/bead-loop/config.toml. Beads in this repo without a work: label (docs, works/) stay in this repo as today. Files: .bead-loop.toml (new), ~/.config/bead-loop/config.toml (outside the repo), README.md (one paragraph: how a pw bead becomes a PR upstream).
acceptance_criteria: bead-supervisor --dry-run work ~/src/preservation-workbench <a work:euclid bead> prints a prompt whose worktree is a fresh worktree of upstream/main in ~/src/euclid; bead-supervisor --local work ~/src/preservation-workbench <that bead> leaves a bead/pw-* branch in ~/src/euclid that passes the configured gate; git -C ~/src/euclids-elements-lektor remote -v shows origin = imkarrer's fork and upstream = brownnrl; nothing is committed to ~/src/euclid or ~/src/euclids-elements-lektor main; git status in this repo shows only .bead-loop.toml and README.md.
notes: blocked on bead-loop bl-wbo (targets epic): bl-mnt, bl-6hg, bl-d01, bl-tka at least must land first

Nelson described it with two screenshots in his #155 comment. Offered to file it; wait for his nod, then file with his screenshots and a reproduction on euclids-elements.org.
acceptance_criteria: Issue exists on brownnrl/euclid with reproduction steps, his screenshots, and a pointer to the relevant plane/rotate code path.
notes: BLOCKED: offered in #155 reply 2026-09-21; waiting for Nelson to say file it.

title: Book IV deck planning tables (16 props) — draft per process.md, do not implement
description: Prepare planning tables for IV.1–IV.16 following euclids-elements-lektor/doc/process.md. Tables are reviewed by Nelson BEFORE implementation. Author in the plain-data discipline (string animation names, no concat, no functions in slides[]). Blocked on his answer to the #155 question for the format; the table drafting itself can proceed.
acceptance_criteria: 16 planning tables in works/euclid-elements/book-iv/, each with slide text carrying Joyce's sentence verbatim, visible/highlighted deltas, animations, justs, and an empty 'Not yet implemented' column or a named geomlib gap.
close_reason: 16 planning tables in works/euclid-elements/book-iv/ (492 lines) + README with conventions, per-prop summary and 6 questions for Nelson. Captions are Joyce's sentences tokenized; slide sets use canonical names; animations in string form; figure additions listed; 'Not yet implemented' filled only where the vocabulary falls short (arc-only highlight, vertex-by-vertex trace). Implementation blocked on his review (pw-kmf).

title: Slideshow presentation feedback: walk Book I-II decks on euclids-elements.org, write up findings
description: Nelson asked for feedback on the slideshow presentation. Spend time with Book I and II decks on the live site (desktop + phone). Note UX observations only — nothing about the narrative. Draft to works/euclid-elements/drafts/, then post as a lektor issue after review.
acceptance_criteria: A drafted issue with concrete, reproducible observations (page, step, device), separated into 'bug' vs 'suggestion'; no prose edits proposed.
close_reason: Draft at works/euclid-elements/drafts/2026-09-21-slideshow-feedback.md: 9 items, each tagged [code] (verified at SlateControls.ts lines cited) or [hands-on]. Two code-verified bugs: Space bound to both reset (canvas) and next (document) while presenting; Next/Prev never disabled at the ends. Not posted — needs Isaac's phone/desktop pass on the [hands-on] items first.

title: geomlib doc PR: string animation names are supported
description: Animations.ts:182 accepts string refs; SlateAnimator and validateSlides route through findAnimation. doc/api.md only shows geomlib.A.* enums. Document the string form with the 14 registered names (note bare 'instant' has no namespace). This is the smallest step of ADR 0002 and stands on its own.
acceptance_criteria: PR against brownnrl/euclid touching docs only; the name table matches the registry at HEAD; a test already covers string names (DiagnosticsTest.ts:317) — cite it in the PR.
close_reason: PR opened: https://github.com/brownnrl/euclid/pull/185 — api.md String names section (14 names, diffed against registry) + pointer in animations-reference.md; docs only.

title: pipeline status: the corpus ledger from the documents, and U3 consistency against the live site
description: Why: tracking is prose upstream and the framework's promise is corpus convergence (delivery-pipeline.md §2.5, §5.7.1, U3). node pipeline/status.mjs reads every document and prints per book: counts by state, documents with stale evidence (pin or lock differs from pipeline/pins.json), documents blocked on library beads (bd dep via bd show --json), mean slides per deck; --write renders the same as a table into works/euclid-elements/README.md between markers. U3: fetch each published document's live page from www.euclids-elements.org, compare <meta name=geomlib-version> to the pin and the slides literal to the document; report every deck live without a document as legacy or unknown. Files: pipeline/status.mjs, works/euclid-elements/README.md (generated block).
acceptance_criteria: npm run status prints the ledger for Book IV documents and the 62 legacy ones; --write produces a deterministic block; U3 against the live site reports 62 legacy decks and zero unknown.

title: Legacy 62 as calibration corpus: reverse-extract Book I and II decks by execution, run P1–P7 and R1–R4, record findings
description: Why: the checks must be calibrated on decks Nelson watched and confirmed before he sees a red gate on Book IV (delivery-pipeline.md §5.7.4, §5.8). The 62 decks compose visible with var and .concat(), so execution is the only honest reader: run each page's script in the check-decks.js vm sandbox against the real bundle and read slates[i].slides, aliases and deferredDraggables back; map enum animation names to strings via the registry's reverse mapping; write works/euclid-elements/decks/legacy/<book>/<prop>.deck.json with state=legacy and no slides[].sentence (P3 falls back to whole-proof matching for legacy). Run P1–P7 and R1–R4 over all 62 in CI on every push. Every finding is either a real defect (file upstream, per his rules) or a false positive that changes the check, documented in the bead's close note; no threshold is tuned without a named case. Files: pipeline/extract-legacy.mjs, works/euclid-elements/decks/legacy/**.
acceptance_criteria: 62 legacy documents committed; npm run check:legacy runs in CI; the close note lists every finding with its disposition; zero unexplained findings remain.

title: GitHub Actions on this repo (L2): setup-node, sibling checkouts at pinned commits, P1–P10 on every document, X2 seeded faults, X3 known-failure expiry, nightly U1 and U3; no flox dependence
description: Why: the corpus converges only if every push re-validates every document and every night re-renders the corpus against geomlib main (delivery-pipeline.md §5.7, §5.10). .github/workflows/checks.yml: on push and pull_request — actions/setup-node 24, npm ci, actions/checkout of brownnrl/euclid at the commit in pipeline/pins.json and brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor at main into sibling paths, npm ci in the euclid checkout (node-canvas from npm; hosted ubuntu has libuuid), then npm run check (P1–P10 on all documents, X2, X3, mermaid, pipeline unit tests). .github/workflows/nightly.yml: schedule — U1 against euclid main with the report as an artifact, U3 ledger consistency. On a pin change (pipeline/pins.json in the diff): X1 re-verification of every implemented+ document. Portability rule from §5.10: no flox in CI; the flox env is for developers and the bead-loop worktree only. Buildkite on ac-box is an optional later optimisation for U1 if hosted runners are too slow.
acceptance_criteria: both workflows green on this branch; a PR that seeds a fault in a Book IV document goes red with the finding in the job summary; the nightly run uploads the U1 report artifact; the workflow file has no flox step.

title: Tier 1 design issue on euclid: solid-geometry animations — Plane.appear, Polyhedron.build, Sphere.appear, Polygon.face as a highlight target
description: Why: today a Book XI table has nothing to put in the Animation column (delivery-pipeline.md §6.2 Tier 1). A design issue before code, per his rule. Body: the constructions the three books use most (table in §6), what each animation would show (parallelogram sweep; faces or edges in declaration order with drawProgress; sphere disc grow), string names in the Type.method shape, args (order, edgesOnly), how each registers declaredNames like compassTransfer does (#159), and snapshot tests following tests/AnimationSnapshotTest.ts. Ask which he wants first. Implementation is a follow-on bead per animation once he answers. Files: works/euclid-elements/drafts/<date>-3d-animations-issue.md, then the issue.
acceptance_criteria: draft in drafts/ reviewed by Isaac; issue opened on brownnrl/euclid; follow-on beads created for the animations he picks, each blocked on this one.

title: Tier 2 design issue on euclid: depth cues, default-off — face sort by centroid depth, lighter back edges, translucent planes, sphere silhouette
description: Why: faces draw in declaration order, planes are flat parallelograms and spheres are discs, so a reader cannot tell front from back (delivery-pipeline.md §6.2 Tier 2). First verify whether translucent planes already work: euclid#179 added an rgb()/rgba() branch to parseColor — try faceColor 'rgba(200,200,200,0.4)' on a plane headlessly and note the result. Then the design issue: an init flag (depthCues: true, default false) that sorts polyhedron faces by centroid z per frame and draws back edges lighter or dashed; the off case bit-for-bit unchanged (his additive rule); goldens with the flag on. Files: works/euclid-elements/drafts/<date>-depth-cues-issue.md, then the issue.
acceptance_criteria: rgba finding recorded in the doc §6.2; issue opened; the answer determines whether an implementation bead is created.

title: 3D audit: which 2D animations and angle markers already work in oblique planes; commit a shared baseline for the XI–XIII fixtures
description: Why: a Book XI planning table cannot promise an Animation column entry nobody has run in 3D (delivery-pipeline.md §6.1). Headlessly, on three XI fixtures with oblique planes: run Point.appear, Line.straightEdgeConnect, Circle.compass (on a circle whose AP is not the screen plane), and angleMarker at a plane foot; record whether each renders where the resting figure does. Snapshot goldens for the three books are gitignored upstream; render them and store them in this repo (pipeline/goldens/euclid-0.16.0/3d/) so 3D has a shared baseline before Tier 0 changes anything. Write the findings as a table in docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §6.1 (replace 'need verification'). Files: pipeline/audit-3d.mjs, pipeline/goldens/…, docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md.
acceptance_criteria: the §6.1 bullet on animations names each of the four as works / does not, with the fixture and PNG that shows it; goldens committed with the euclid commit hash in the directory name.

title: .agents/skills/deck-authoring: lektor/doc/process.md in the form the bead-loop worker reads
description: Why: the worker that drafts a deck document needs Nelson's authoring rules, not just his fidelity rules (pw-xl2 covers those). Under 80 lines: the planning-table workflow; the fatigue rule; only the proposition canvas gets slides except guide-proofs; captions are Joyce's sentence split not compressed; canonical names only in slide sets; deferDraggables vs vertex points (II.3 lesson); zero-colour targets and explicit ;0 face colour; the animation catalogue by string name; where the deck document lives and which pipeline commands prove it. Same frontmatter check as pw-xl2 (~/src/bead-loop/test/lint-skills.sh). Files: .agents/skills/deck-authoring/SKILL.md.
acceptance_criteria: lint-skills passes; every rule cites a process.md heading or a deck-tracker.md row; a dry-run prompt from bead-supervisor --dry-run shows the skill linked.

title: Deck beads generated from the corpus inventory: one per proposition, chained per book, library gaps filed as blockers
description: Why: the unit of work is a proposition and nothing carries its state (delivery-pipeline.md §5). Generate bd create commands (dry-run first) for the 403 propositions without slides: title '<Book>.<n> deck: <statement…>', labels delegate:local, work:lektor, book:<roman>, description pointing at the deck document path and the process, acceptance = plan checks + narrative-diff + check-decks + contact sheet exist. Chain with bd dep in proposition order within a book and in Nelson's order across books (lektor #21–#31: III first). A not_yet_implemented entry in a document files a euclid-target bead and adds a dep. Only Book III and IV beads are actually created in this bead; the rest stay as a generator run with --dry-run until the pipeline has landed one book. Depends on pw-j4m (targets) for the loop to run them. Files: pipeline/gen-beads.mjs.
acceptance_criteria: bd ready shows exactly one Book III deck bead (III.1) and Book IV's first; bd blocked shows the rest chained; the dry-run for all 403 is pasted (count only) in the close note.
notes: Revised 2026-09-21 per delivery-pipeline.md §3.3: TWO beads per proposition — a plan bead (default target, writes the .deck.json, gate G1) and an implement bead (lektor target, runs the generator, gates G2+G3+D1/D2/D5), the implement bead blocked on the plan bead and on a per-book H1 marker bead the operator closes when Nelson approves the tables. Library-gap beads on the euclid target block the implement bead.

title: Upstream: GitHub Actions on the lektor repo running check-decks, check-versions and check-subjindex on every PR
description: Why: the content repo has no CI (no .github/); its three publish gates run on the publisher's laptop (delivery-pipeline.md §2.2, §3.4 item 1). Ask first: a short issue on brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor offering it. Workflow: checkout, node 24, python 3, npm ci of @brownnrl/geomlib at the pin read from templates/layout.html plus canvas, then the three scripts. check-decks.js reads dist/bundle.js from EUCLID_REPO — either pass a directory containing node_modules/@brownnrl/geomlib/dist as EUCLID_REPO or add an optional bundle-path env in the same PR (say which in the PR body). No lektor build in CI in the first cut. Files (in the lektor worktree): .github/workflows/checks.yml; possibly scripts/check-decks.js (one env var).
acceptance_criteria: the workflow passes on a branch of our fork against upstream main; the PR on brownnrl/euclids-elements-lektor is opened only after Nelson answers the issue; if he declines, the workflow stays on our fork and the bead is closed with that note.
notes: Revised 2026-09-21: his repo, his call. Offer the workflow in an issue first; package our checks so any one of them is an npx line he can add or ignore. If he declines, the workflow lives on our fork only.

title: Corpus visual run and pin-bump impact report: every figure and slide under a candidate geomlib bundle, diffed against goldens
description: Why: the 0.16 bump surfaced 70 diagnostics on 21 untouched pages at pin time (delivery-pipeline.md §4). Using the per-slide renderer: walk all contents.lr with geomlib.init (726 figures; 465 proposition pages), render every figure and every slide under bundle A (current pin) and bundle B (candidate: a euclid checkout at a ref), pixel-diff, and write a markdown report grouped by page with diff images, plus diagnostics deltas. Goldens per (deck, geomlib version, flox env) under pipeline/goldens/ or a release asset — decide and record in the doc §9. Depends on the headless renderer bead. Files: pipeline/corpus-run.mjs, pipeline/report.mjs, docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §9 (decision).
acceptance_criteria: running against euclid 0.15.x vs 0.16.0 reproduces the 21-page/70-diagnostic finding from lektor PR #37 in the report; wall time for the full corpus is recorded in the close note.

title: Generator: approved deck document → contents.lr edit (figure additions, slides literal, aliases, eucrefs map)
description: Why: with the document as source, implementation becomes codegen (delivery-pipeline.md §3.3 Generate). Emit into the existing <script> of the target canvas: appended figure_additions strings, aliases, deferDraggables, a slides array as a JSON-parseable literal (string animation names, no .concat(), no functions in slides[]), the resolveJustification function and window.eucrefs map generated from the refs via the same resolver rules the plan check uses. Idempotent: running twice yields no diff. Runs narrative-diff and lektor/scripts/check-decks.js afterwards (EUCLID_REPO from the flox env). Depends on the deck document bead. Files: pipeline/generate.mjs, pipeline/test/generate.test.mjs.
acceptance_criteria: for propIV1: generated contents.lr passes narrative-diff against the original, passes node check-decks.js with zero issues, JSON.parse succeeds on the extracted slides literal, and a second run produces an empty git diff.

title: Headless per-slide renderer and contact sheet from the euclid source checkout
description: Why: nothing looks at rendered slides except a person (delivery-pipeline.md §2.4, §3.3 Render). Build a slate from the page's figure with ts-node against ../euclid/src the way tests/SnapshotHelper.ts does (the npm bundle exports neither Slate nor computeSlideState — docs/research/geomlib-internals.md §3.4); for each slide apply computeSlideState + setVisibleNames + highlights, render with node-canvas to PNG, run the per-slide assertions (every highlighted element defined and visible; every animated elem visible on its slide; visible non-empty), collect diagnostics with 'at' dropped, and compose a contact sheet PNG per deck with captions. One deck per process (GeomElement.setFont is process-global). Files: pipeline/render-deck.mjs, pipeline/contact-sheet.mjs, .gitignore for pipeline/out/.
acceptance_criteria: node pipeline/render-deck.mjs <contents.lr> canvas_0 writes N slide PNGs and one contact sheet for propI5 (18 slides) in under 10 s, exits non-zero when a slide's highlighted element is hidden (seeded), and two runs produce byte-identical PNGs.

title: Tier 3 design issue on euclid: per-slide view and an A.View.orbit transition (model rotation now, camera after the renderer split)
description: Why: turning the solid between slides is the point of a 3D walk and nothing in ISlide names a view (delivery-pipeline.md §6.2 Tier 3). Depends on Tier 0 (rotation must be rigid first). Issue body: a view field on ISlide (rotation angle about the pivot axis in the pivot plane), the orbit transition as an animation over Slate.rotateCoordinates-style rigid rotation, reset() semantics (construction coordinates already restored), how computeSlideState stays pure, and why a camera waits for the kernel/renderer split (PLAN.md P4). Files: works/euclid-elements/drafts/<date>-view-orbit-issue.md, then the issue.
acceptance_criteria: issue opened after Tier 0 has merged; the doc §6.2 Tier 3 row links it.

title: Work descriptor: what the pipeline parameterizes for Apollonius and Hilbert (docs/design/delivery-pipeline.md §7)
